content.title: About
content.content: Green pickled cabbage is a fermented product made from fresh white cabbage leaves that are submerged in a brine with salt, spices, and sometimes carrots. It has a distinctive tangy‑salty flavor, crisp texture, and a fragrant aroma. The product is commonly used as a side dish, snack, or ingredient in salads and Eastern‑style recipes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fermented cabbage is a traditional staple in many Eastern European and Asian cuisines.
Fermentation increases the vitamin C content compared with fresh cabbage.
Typical brine acidity ranges from 2.5 % to 3.0 %, allowing long‑term storage without refrigeration.
Lactic‑acid bacteria such as Lactobacillus develop during fermentation, providing probiotic benefits.
When kept in a sealed jar, it can stay good for up to 12 months at room temperature if fully submerged in brine.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: The acidic fermentation makes vitamin C more bioavailable, supporting immunity and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Probiotic bacteria formed during fermentation promote a healthy gut microbiome and aid digestion.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Cabbage is low in calories but high in dietary fiber, which helps with weight management.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: It provides potassium, calcium, and magnesium, essential for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phenolic compounds in cabbage help combat free radicals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The large amount of salt may be unsuitable for people with hypertension or kidney disease.

items.title: Cabbage allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cabbage or fermented products.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improper storage or incomplete fermentation can allow growth of harmful bacteria.

items.title: Stomach sensitivity
items.content: The acidity may cause discomfort for those with gastritis or ulcer disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: It can be enjoyed straight from the jar, added to sandwiches, salads, soups, stews, or used as a side for meat dishes. Often it is rinsed briefly to reduce excess brine before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dark place in an airtight jar. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 1–2 months. Discard if mold appears or an off‑smell develops.
